title: Shooting a laser at the galactic center
caption: A laser aimed at the galactic center from the Very Large Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Two of the 8.2-meter telescopes of ESO's Very Large Telescope stand against the myriad stars and dust of the Milky Way in this view of the sky above Paranal on 21 July 2007. Just above Yepun, Unit Telescope number 4, shines the Small Magellanic Cloud, a satellite galaxy of the Milky Way.

A laser beam streams out of Yepun toward the center of our galaxy. It has a practical purpose, helping the telescope obtain images free from the blurring caused by Earth's atmosphere. The beam looks slightly artificial, a side effect of saturation during the long exposure.
The brightest object, at upper right, is the planet Jupiter, sitting next to the star Antares. The image was taken by ESO astronomer Yuri Beletsky.

understand.summary: This is a long-exposure photograph of the sky over Paranal. The source gives no camera or exposure details beyond that.
understand.eye: The long exposure gathers far more light than the eye, and saturation makes the laser beam look slightly artificial.

explore: Saturation happens when a camera receives more light than it can record, so the brightest parts of an image lose detail.
alt: Two VLT telescopes under the Milky Way, one firing a laser beam, with the Small Magellanic Cloud above and Jupiter bright at upper right.
